passage:
Every day, Mr. Lin took the train to work. He always sat by the window and looked at the same fields, houses, and roads.
One morning, the window was dirty, and he could not see clearly. He felt annoyed. Then he noticed his reflection in the glass. He looked tired.
That evening, instead of looking out, he closed his eyes and rested. The next day, he brought a book. The day after that, he talked with an old friend he met on the train.
When the window was cleaned, Mr. Lin enjoyed the view again. But he no longer needed it every day.
A dirty window had changed his habit. Sometimes losing one small comfort helps people find other ways to use time.
